premise: Every historical smart-mode result with hierarchy depth L >= 2 is provisional until replaced or explicitly retained only as historical context.

common.full_baseline_reuse_policy: Reuse is admissible only when source, protocol, bootstrap, graph representation, hardware, and principal clock hashes match exactly; this queue schedules one fresh paired long run by default.

hard_stop_rules: Stop before measurements unless the repaired production API is explicitly acknowledged and unit tests pass.
Stop the entire queue on any production Stage 1 hierarchy-refinement failure, label-namespace collision across an affected-scope boundary, or write outside the full-method audited scope.
Stop before mechanism profiles unless the instrumented full variant reproduces production launcher final modularity and NMI within 1e-6.

Run the radius-only scope control only as a discarded one-step clone of the production pre-update state; require collision-free labels, strict nesting, and preservation of the partition relation outside the scope, while recording numeric outside relabeling separately.
Stop and start a new campaign if optimizer, launcher, profiler, audit, config, or validation source hashes change.
Never suppress a failed run or replace an unfavorable valid result; failed attempts and negative outcomes remain in the campaign.
scientific_decision_rules: Stages 1-4 are the core evidence and take precedence over every optional control.

After Stage 2, retain valid results even if repaired ComNetX is slower or lower quality. If neither large graph has speedup above one with Delta Q >= -0.05, skip optional breadth experiments and reframe the empirical claim instead of tuning on the test streams.
Stage 5 may start only when at least 38 hours remain, preserving a 30-hour slot for the 26.95 GPU-hour DSBM queue plus validation margin.

Stage 6 may start only when at least 30 hours remain. If it cannot start, record it as skipped_for_budget rather than deleting the existing DSBM section or silently presenting old smart rows as repaired results.
Stage 7 backend-interface rows are last and cannot displace Stages 1-4 or the reserved DSBM slot.

claim_mapping.RQ1: Stages 1, 2, and 4 establish repaired Leiden quality and update-time behavior on real streams.
claim_mapping.RQ2: The separate LD-Leiden pack is the principal comparator; Stage 7 restores repaired DF-Leiden and S2CAG interface rows.
claim_mapping.RQ3: Stage 3 production-backed phase and workload profiles quantify inspected scopes and backend quotient sizes.
claim_mapping.RQ4: Stage 3 radius-only-scope and vertex-level-base-atom ablations plus Stage 5 topology, direction, cut, and resolution controls identify causal design choices.
claim_mapping.RQ5: Stage 4 long-horizon repeatability, Stage 6 DSBM update-rate/type controls, and the late feature-input control test robustness and operating boundaries.

stages.purpose: All-six repaired Leiden smoke plus real-stream hierarchy and namespace audits.
Five paired fixed-input repetitions of repaired ComNetX and warm-start full Leiden on both large graphs.
Production/profile parity gate followed by repaired closure and contraction profiles.
One fresh paired 9:500 run per large graph.
Up to two additional repaired smart-only 9:500 repetitions as budget allows.
Depth/radius grid first, then direction, cut, and resolution controls without consuming the DSBM reserve.
Preserved late queue of 30 repaired smart DSBM runs over three update types, two rates, and five seeds.
Five repaired DF-Leiden smart short repetitions plus one smart-only 9:500 coverage run needed to retain the long-horizon interface row.
One to five repaired S2CAG smart interface repetitions plus the retained dataset/random/one-hot feature-input control.
